    carries NotEqual and an O-09 of two positional `graph_child` arguments, each the literal's own node with empty
    Bounds and no parameter position.
- id: FR-033-AC-15
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-033-composite-parity-replay-binding.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-814). When the original application node is a `structural.ne` comparing one parameter with
    itself and the requested operator is NotEqual, the verified request carries NotEqual and an O-09 of two positional
    `graph_child` arguments with the same node identity, each retaining the drawn Node-keyed bounds naming that
    parameter and neither deduplicated.
- id: FR-033-AC-16
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-033-composite-parity-replay-binding.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-814; verified by Inspection of the single conversion that AC-17 tests). If the owning operand
    projection refuses an inline integer literal operand (`InlineInteger`), then the builder returns that refusal
    through `CompositeBuildError::Operands` before any QSL invocation, with no report or terminal value and no built
    argument. The owning contract treats this branch as defensive because reader admission already refuses an integer
    operand of `structural.eq` and `structural.ne`, so no admitted fixture can reach it. Both inline refusals pass
    through the same
- id: FR-033-AC-17
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-033-composite-parity-replay-binding.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-814). If the owning operand projection refuses an inline non-integer literal operand (`InlineNonInteger`),
    then the builder returns that refusal through `CompositeBuildError::Operands` before any QSL invocation, with
    no report or terminal value and no new CG error variant. No test of this path exists yet.
- id: FR-019-AC-1
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Settlement dispatches one arm per variant of the closed backend kind, and every variant reaches an arm
    that settles rather than falling through.
- id: FR-019-AC-2
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Every requested item receives exactly one of `supported`, `requires-bound`, `unsupported` and `invalid-request`,
    settled from its `candidates` and extent classification, and `candidates` is read from the request rather than
    computed here.
- id: FR-019-AC-3
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: On the Kani arm, an unbounded extent against a `bounded`-only advertisement settles `requires-bound`
    when a finite bound is available, rather than `unsupported`; with no finite bound available it settles `unsupported`,
    warned, with `unsupported_projection`/`unbounded-extent`; and it never settles `supported`.
- id: FR-019-AC-4
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: An item with more than one candidate and no named backend settles `invalid-request` with `invalid_capability`/`ambiguous-backend`,
    naming every candidate in candidate order, identically under every registration order.
- id: FR-019-AC-10
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Only an item settled `supported` routes.
- id: FR-019-AC-45
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: 'A manifest with a second descriptor of one backend identity causes a whole-envelope `EnvelopeRefusal::ManifestRepeatsBackendIdentity
    { identity: String }`, whether the descriptors are identical, differ in `ProviderOrigin` alone, or differ in
    any other CG descriptor field, and whether adjacent or non-adjacent. The call returns no item settlements. The
    variant has no string cause, manifest or digest payload; `negotiate_backend_provider` keeps its return signature.'
- id: FR-019-AC-46
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: With several repeated identities, the refusal names the bytewise-first repeated identity independent
    of manifest order; identities differing only in case are distinct. An invalid contract version or capability
    vocabulary is refused as `EnvelopeRefusal::InvalidCapability` before repeat detection or any kind read.
- id: FR-019-AC-47
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: QSL's registry snapshot holds each backend identity at most once (FR-290:258-265; FR-331:57), so no driver-built
    FR-331 manifest repeats an identity.
- id: FR-019-AC-48
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: 'A `Refused(refusal)` outcome from the current Kani oracle-function preflight read produces `Err(EnvelopeRefusal::ContractPackageReadRefused
    { refusal: ContractPackageRefusalProjection })` for the whole request, with the reader''s `code`, `path`, `cause`,
    `locus`, `contract_version`, `document_pointer`, `expected` and `actual` copied into the named CG projection;
    the private `expected_node_id` is absent. No item settlement or artifact is returned.'
- id: FR-019-AC-49
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: 'An `Incomplete(incomplete)` outcome from the current Kani oracle-function preflight read produces `Err(EnvelopeRefusal::ContractPackageReadIncomplete
    { incomplete: ContractPackageIncompleteProjection })` for the whole request, with the reader''s `limit_kind`,
    `limit`, `consumed` and `path` copied into the named CG projection. No item settlement or artifact is returned.'
- id: FR-019-AC-50
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: An `Admitted` Kani function-application preflight read whose exact generator produces a claim for an
    otherwise supported item retains the existing `supported` settlement.
- id: FR-019-AC-51
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Among several request items with non-`Admitted` preflight outcomes, the first failing item in manifest/item
    request order determines the whole-request `ContractPackageReadRefused` or `ContractPackageReadIncomplete` variant
    and projection, irrespective of outcome kind. Earlier successful items contribute no returned settlement or
    artifact.
- id: FR-019-AC-52
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: An `Admitted` Kani function-application read whose exact generator emits no claim, and a structural preflight
    rejection before any read, each retain item-level `KaniFormRefused { OperationNotRendered }` without a reader
    envelope refusal.
- id: FR-019-AC-53
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Given an admitted package with bound driver items at driver indexes 0 and 2 around an excluded accounting-only
    position at index 1 whose accounting is `lowered` with a Kani-supported form, an FR-331 envelope with exactly
    two items settles the bound items without an `EnvelopeItemCount` refusal. Both `ContractItemSettlement.request_index`
    and its nested `ItemSettlement.request_index` equal 0 and 2 respectively, not envelope indexes 0 and 1. The
    excluded position produces no settlement or claim, and its own classifier-call and Kani-preflight-read counts
    are both zero. An envelope with fewer
- id: FR-019-AC-7
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: An envelope whose `capability_vocabulary` is not exactly `quire.capability-kind/v1`, or is absent, is
    refused as `invalid_capability`/`unsupported-version` with none of its kinds read.
- id: FR-019-AC-8
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: An item with an absent extent classification settles `invalid-request` with `invalid_capability`/`absent-extent`,
    and an absent or unknown kind settles before the candidate table is consulted.
- id: FR-019-AC-9
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: 'A backend kind added without a negotiation arm does not compile: the dispatch is an exhaustive `match`
    over the closed kind with no catch-all arm.'
- id: FR-019-AC-11
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). `BackendKind` has `Process(id)` beside `Kani`; `ALL` lists finite built-in kinds only,
    while CG enumerates process candidates from descriptors. CG's descriptor-to-kind conversion returns `Process(id)`
    exactly when a descriptor has process origin, including identity text `kani`. A named, registered process backend
    reaches that arm and receives one disposition; no process item disappears for being absent from `ALL`.
- id: FR-019-AC-12
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629; non-empty bounded rows depend on QSL-654's producer and admit-side enforcement). A bounded
    process item with an uncovered `extent.bounds[].kind` settles `unsupported`, warned, with `unsupported_projection`/`unsupported-requested-capability`
    naming the offending domain kind and candidate (QSpec FR-290-AC-13). An item that passes the domain check, including
    one with empty `bounds`, settles `supported` exactly when its descriptor advertises `bounded` for its kind;
    otherwise it settles `unsupported`, warned, with `unsupported_projection`/`unsupported-requested-capability`.
- id: FR-019-AC-16
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). An unbounded process item settles `supported` when its descriptor advertises `unbounded`
    for its kind, regardless of whether any `extent.domains[].kind` belongs to manifest `domains`.
- id: FR-019-AC-17
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). On a `bounded`-only process descriptor, an unbounded item settles `requires-bound`
    exactly when `finite_bound_available` is true and every boundable `extent.domains[].kind` is in manifest `domains`
    (QSpec FR-290-AC-13).
- id: FR-019-AC-18
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). Given the same process advertisements and item extent, changing only backend identity,
    manifest position, manifest run-limit defaults or ambient state leaves the disposition and cause unchanged apart
    from the backend named in the output.
- id: FR-019-AC-19
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629; bounded row depends on QSL-654's producer). The process arm reads each explicit `extent.bounds[].kind`
    and never derives a domain kind from `DomainKey`; two otherwise equal bounded items with the same `DomainKey`
    and different explicit kinds can settle differently under one manifest `domains` set.
- id: FR-019-AC-20
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629; driver projection remains paired work). CG's process descriptor retains the FR-331 manifest's
    advertised (kind, mode) pairs, `domains` and optional `bounds` beside the IR-633 `id` and `origin` projection.
- id: FR-019-AC-42
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Two otherwise equal CG Process descriptors with absent and present-empty manifest `bounds` remain distinct
    typed values. Changing only between those forms leaves process settlement's disposition and request-validation
    precedence unchanged; run-limit defaults are not proof bounds.
- id: FR-019-AC-21
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). On a `bounded`-only process descriptor, an unbounded item with any unadvertised boundable
    `extent.domains[].kind` settles `unsupported`, warned, with `unsupported_projection`/`unsupported-requested-capability`
    naming the offending domain kind and candidate, regardless of `finite_bound_available`; non-boundable kinds
    are not compared (QSpec FR-290-AC-13).
- id: FR-019-AC-22
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629). On a `bounded`-only process descriptor, an unbounded item with every boundable `extent.domains[].kind`
    advertised and the item's `finite_bound_available=false` settles `unsupported`, warned, with `unsupported_projection`/`unbounded-extent`.
    CG reads that flag from the item and does not derive it from the domain kinds (QSpec FR-290-AC-13).
- id: FR-019-AC-23
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629; bounded row depends on QSL-654). Changing only a bounded item's proof-bound numeric
    maximum leaves its process-provider `supported` or `unsupported` disposition and cause unchanged.
- id: FR-019-AC-13
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: 'Settling a process-provider item reaches no plugin: a descriptor whose identity names a non-existent
    executable settles identically to one with an ordinary identity, apart from the backend each names, and starts
    nothing, and a descriptor whose identity names an executable that records its own start leaves no record. A
    mutant arm that starts or resolves the identity as a process either changes the first disposition or leaves
    the record, and fails this.'
- id: FR-019-AC-14
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: The process-provider arm's return type is `Disposition`, which has no terminal-value, verification-result
    or artifact member, so settling returns none of them. A change that returns one does not compile against that
    type.
- id: FR-019-AC-15
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-633). CG's `BackendDescriptor` has a typed `ProviderOrigin` projecting exactly QSL layer
    R's `Linked` and `Process` meanings (QSL FR-288, ADR-029 PV-1); layer R owns that vocabulary. The driver projects
    each descriptor from `Registry::descriptors()` once into CG's descriptor, copying `id` and advertised pairs
    unchanged and mapping `origin()` exhaustively, `Linked` to `Linked` and `Process` to `Process`, with no wildcard
    or origin inference from identity, manifest or provider bytes or a side map. Two registry descriptors identical
    except for origin produce CG descriptors
- id: FR-019-AC-24
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: 'PLANNED (IR-338). Given QSL FR-335''s `value-validity` claim rooted at an unbounded `s: Set<Int[0,9999]>`,
    an empty candidate registry settles `unsupported` with a warning naming `value-validity` and emits no artifact
    or Kani outcome; one linked Kani candidate advertising (`value-validity`, `bounded`) with `finite_bound_available=true`
    settles the unbounded item `requires-bound` without substituting a bound or emitting an artifact; a separately
    requested bounded `ProofBound::Cardinality{maximum: 8}` item with that same sole candidate settles `supported`
    under its own request index, while'
- id: FR-019-AC-25
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: 'The normative Kani form set is the complete V1 proof set defined by IR-269 and FR-015: scalar families
    Boolean, integer, rational, decimal, IEEE float, text, enum and quantity; record and tuple composite equality;
    function application; precondition, postcondition and invariant `BoundClause` roles; and bounded collection
    and graph forms. V1 `ClauseKind` has no frame variant. State before/after and frame obligations are typed V2
    `StateFrame` items with the `contract` or `frame` role, included where FR-015 defines their typed lowering.
    Each item is identified by its typed IR tag/form,'
- id: FR-019-AC-26
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: For any form in FR-019-AC-25 with one validated Kani candidate, a bounded extent settles `supported`
    exactly when the form's FR-015 lowering succeeds and the candidate advertises the bounded mode; negotiation
    creates no artifact as part of settlement.
- id: FR-019-AC-27
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: With one Kani candidate, a typed form outside the normative set in FR-019-AC-25 settles `unsupported`,
    warned, with `unsupported_projection`/`unsupported-requested-capability` naming its typed tag/form and Kani;
    no artifact is emitted and no generator is invoked. A malformed in-set form settles with the applicable typed
    FR-015 validation refusal.
- id: FR-019-AC-33
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: For a valid bounded typed form inside FR-019-AC-25 that matches one specific Planned subpath in TC-030's
    status register and does not match an Implemented subpath, negotiation returns `unsupported` with that subpath's
    single exact typed refusal cause, emits no artifact, and never settles `supported` before its renderer is implemented;
    this refusal remains distinct from the out-of-V1 refusal in AC-27.
- id: FR-019-AC-28
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: A form refusal under FR-019-AC-27 is distinct from an empty candidate set, which retains the missing-capability
    cause, and from multiple candidates without a named backend, which retains `invalid_capability`/`ambiguous-backend`
    naming each candidate in candidate order.
- id: FR-019-AC-29
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: After request and candidate/manifest validation select one Kani candidate, Kani checks the typed IR form
    before its extent and advertised-mode rules; if both the form and mode/extent are unsupported, the form refusal
    of FR-019-AC-27 settles the item.
- id: FR-019-AC-30
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: For the same typed IR tag/form, changing only its display or debug text leaves Kani's disposition, cause
    and named form identity unchanged.
- id: FR-019-AC-31
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: For a Kani-supported unbounded form against a `bounded`-only advertisement, `finite_bound_available=true`
    settles `requires-bound`, with no substituted bound and no artifact.
- id: FR-019-AC-32
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: When a caller supplies a finite bound in a new bounded request for a Kani-supported form, negotiation
    settles `supported` and preserves the exact supplied proof-bound value, domain kind and domain identity.
- id: FR-019-AC-34
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). With one EN-1 candidate, an advertised admitted TP-1 through TP-4, TP-5, SG-1 through
    SG-3, or HP-1 model/HP-2/HP-3/HP-6 form settles through its explicit-state arm with the recorded form and model-or-protocol
    subject intact; an unadvertised form or HP-1 code claim does not settle `supported` through EN-1.
- id: FR-019-AC-35
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). With one SMT temporal candidate advertising the item's kind and form, TP-1 through
    TP-4 route only to an EN-2 or EN-3 method ADR-018 assigns to that form and subject; TP-4 does not route to EN-3,
    and a form absent from the candidate's advertised form set settles `unsupported` with no engine request.
- id: FR-019-AC-36
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). A TP-5 whole-refinement `temporal-satisfaction` item retains its safety and optional
    liveness halves on the concrete subject through EN-1, and the same whole item reaches an advertising SMT arm
    for RE-3 refutation; a separately requested RE-2 `operation-contract` item reaches the SMT arm for per-step
    safety checking, but its disposition cannot substitute for the whole-refinement item. An arm lacking the required
    TP-5 form settles the item `unsupported`.
- id: FR-019-AC-37
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). HP-1 model, HP-2, HP-3 and HP-6 reach an advertising EN-1 arm; only HP-2 reaches an
    advertising SMT arm under its applicable EN-2 or EN-3 method. HP-4 and an unadvertised HP form settle unsupported
    before an engine, HP-5 stays on its possible-property path, and an HP-1 code claim is not settled as an EN-1
    model claim.
- id: FR-019-AC-38
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). An advertised SG-1, SG-2 or SG-3 item reaches EN-1 with its recorded form; only advertised
    SG-1 reaches an SMT arm. SG-2 or SG-3 against an SMT-only candidate settles unsupported and reaches no SMT engine.
- id: FR-019-AC-39
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). A selected reduction reaches only a candidate advertising that exact reduction, with
    the selection preserved in the routed request. Symmetry declarations and POR enter the obligation identity,
    so their reduced and unreduced requests for one claim have distinct obligation identities; a state constraint
    changes request identity but leaves obligation identity unchanged. An unadvertised selection or POR on a subject
    with no footprints settles `unsupported` without an artifact, and no arm drops or adds a reduction.
- id: FR-019-AC-40
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). For an item over a weak `parallel`, a candidate advertising the subject's resolved
    `tso` or `ra` model receives that exact model; a candidate lacking it settles `unsupported` with no artifact,
    and no arm weakens the resolved model. An `sc` subject is a separate strong-model control and does not take
    the weak-memory branch.
- id: FR-019-AC-41
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-516). With otherwise equal form and kind advertisement, model and protocol subject classes
    are read separately; an arm that discharges only one class settles the other `unsupported`, while a supported
    protocol item retains its protocol transition-system subject identity through routing.
- id: FR-019-AC-43
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Two driver items selecting distinct `expression` occurrences of one checked `integer.add` node and different
    direct `numeric.narrow` occurrences in one admitted ContractPackage settle independently under the same Kani
    descriptor. Each preflight result is classified from its own selected result context; changing the selected
    narrow changes that item's typed result identity or refusal without changing the other. A node-only classifier
    or package-wide choice of either bound fails this control.
- id: FR-019-AC-44
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: For a V2 scalar claim, an absent `OwnResult`, an application occurrence absent from the admitted source,
    a conversion occurrence from another source or unrelated to the application, a missing conversion context root,
    or a ContractPackage source identity different from the checked source settles `invalid-request` with a typed
    form/context cause and no artifact or harness. Request and candidate/manifest defects retain their earlier precedence;
    for a valid candidate this selected-form refusal precedes extent and advertised-mode refusal. Neither a source
    message nor a caller maximum repairs
- id: FR-022-AC-1
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Generation dispatches one arm per variant of the closed `BackendKind` through an exhaustive `match` with
    no catch-all, and `GenerationContexts::has` handles each variant; adding a variant without either arm does not
    compile. `Process` requires no context.
- id: FR-022-AC-2
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: For a set of routed Kani items, each record and harness in the output equals what `negotiate_kani_obligations`
    returns for the same items in ascending request-index order with the same context. The one difference is that
    every index inside a record is the driver's request index, and each harness is paired with the record whose
    `harness_symbol` names it.
- id: FR-022-AC-3
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: The entry point accepts no backend registry, candidate set, extent or capability kind, and constructs
    no FR-019 `Disposition`.
- id: FR-022-AC-4
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: PLANNED (IR-629 internal-invariant test migration). A crate-internal malformed routed Kani item whose
    private backend identity has no CG built-in kind, or converts to a kind other than Kani, refuses the whole call
    as `BackendKindDisagrees`, naming the request index, backend, routed kind and converted kind or its absence,
    with no artifact.
- id: FR-022-AC-5
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Two routed items with one request index refuse as `DuplicateRequestIndex` naming it. A routed Kani item
    without Kani context refuses as `MissingKindContext` naming Kani. Each returns no artifact.
- id: FR-022-AC-6
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: A Kani group-level refusal (for example an unwind outside `1..=1024`, or an unparsable subject path)
    is returned as `Kani` carrying the unchanged `KaniObligationError`, with no artifact.
- id: FR-022-AC-7
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: A Kani group containing an `invalid_request` item is listed in `rejected`, and every Kani item's record
    is returned with no harness. A `DuplicateItem` reported by FR-015 has `first_index` rewritten to the driver's
    request index of the first occurrence. On the FR-330 package path, an identical selected scalar occurrence pair
    also retains FR-039's earlier typed `DuplicateRequest` claim refusal at both positions.
- id: FR-022-AC-8
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Every routed item appears exactly once in `items`, in ascending request index, under its routed backend
    and the `KindOutput` variant of its routed kind. An item the arm refuses at lowering keeps its typed FR-015
    refusal and no harness. An empty routed set returns an empty result.
- id: FR-022-AC-9
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined
  excerpt: Regeneration from equal inputs is byte-identical, and a permutation of the routed-item slice yields an
    identical result. The same node routed at a different request index or under another candidate of the same backend
    yields a byte-identical harness when the admitted FR-330 package and selected occurrence are the same.
- id: FR-022-AC-10
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined

  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: examined

    QSL path guard: the same guard occurrence with `holds=true` for the then item and `holds=false` for the else
    item. CG preserves the full outermost-first guard sequence and uses it when forming the proof obligation; a
    result under `p=false` cannot prove the then claim and one under `p=true` cannot prove the else claim. An empty
    path condition remains unguarded.'
- id: FR-022-AC-28
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md

- id: AD-001
  path: spec/assurance/AD-001-codegen-architecture.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The code generator turns an admitted contract package into Rust oracles, property-test harnesses,

    bounded Kani obligations and their evidence, runs one Kani obligation on the installed backend,

    and hands every counterexample to QSL for native replay. It is the Kani backend adapter of the

    AD-016 pipeline: it selects the runtime operation per IR node at arrow 3, settles capabilities at

    arrow 4''s single negotiation point and generates oracles there, generates harnesses at arrow 5, and

    owns the execution half of arrow 6 and the reconstruction half of arrow 7.'
- id: AD-002
  path: spec/assurance/AD-002-cg-qsl-replay-seam.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The Replay subsystem row of the Subsystem Registry lists this AD beside AD-001. It is a view of

    one boundary of AD-001''s "CG to QSL" seam rows, not a second architecture, and it is one of the

    seam descriptions of IR-324. The evidence chain that joins this seam to IR and to the terminal

    value is [AD-003](AD-003-evidence-chain.md).'
- id: AD-003
  path: spec/assurance/AD-003-evidence-chain.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'This AD governs the Kani and Evidence subsystems and the Replay subsystem''s identity members. CG

    owns it because CG is the one repository that depends on both IR and QSL; IR must not depend on

    QSL, so no other repository can join the chain. IR and QSL each hold their own link and are cited,

    not copied. It is one of the seam descriptions of IR-324.'
- id: AD-004
  path: spec/assurance/AD-004-cg-crate-layout.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'AD-001 states what the generator is and which seams it has. This AD states how `src/` is cut so

    that the code matches the subsystems in the Subsystem Registry of [spec.md](../spec.md): the

    directory tree, which module goes where, which way imports may point, and what is deleted. It is

    the design that IR-348 implements. It describes this repository only. Seams to IR, RT and QSL are

    AD-001''s. The replay seam (AD-002) and the evidence chain (AD-003) are the seam descriptions of

    IR-324; both are merged, and this AD references them.'
- id: AD-005
  path: spec/assurance/AD-005-source-obligation-producer.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'This AD defines the planned [FR-036](../evidence/functional/FR-036-source-obligation-census.md)

    CG producer seam. The source owners supply selected inventories and authored mappings;

    CG exports their complete census and actual producer facts. IR FR-045/AD-008 own

    eligibility, joins, proof credit and the four accounting projections. The driver or

    another adapter above both owners connects the borrowed exports to IR accounting.

    This seam adds no solver, production-source parser or assurance verdict.'
- id: FR-005
  path: spec/core/functional/FR-005-cli-conformance.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When invoked through the library or CLI, the generator shall write a complete artifact bundle

    atomically and shall retain differential and cross-backend semantic-parity results.'
- id: FR-037
  path: spec/core/functional/FR-037-fixture-identity.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When the exact-scalar or composite-equality fixture builder assigns a candidate

    identity to an application-bodied checked-package node, the builder shall use

    Contract IR''s `derive_application_node_id` with an `ApplicationNodeDraft` made

    from that node. For a grouped node, it shall supply an

    `ApplicationIdentityContext` made from the complete, ordered draft graph. The

    builder shall use the resulting candidate node ID for fixture assembly and

    retain the checked-package reader as the admission authority. It shall not

    construct or hash a local copy of the application preimage or its version tag.'
- id: FR-038
  path: spec/core/functional/FR-038-typed-operator-catalog.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: "When a V2 oracle or Kani generator selects an operation from an IR-admitted\nchecked-package claim,\
    \ Contract Codegen shall resolve its catalogued identity\nthrough one internal, closed typed operator source.\
    \ That source shall describe\nthe operation family, operand arity and order, result kind, and applicable\nrendering\
    \ metadata without becoming an authority for IR admission or inventing\nan identity absent from the upstream\
    \ verification catalog. Each consumer shall\nselect only the operations it can render and shall retain its existing\
    \ typed\n  refusal or unsupported disposition for an"
- id: FR-039
  path: spec/core/functional/FR-039-contract-package-consumption.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When the driver submits a complete-V1 request for production negotiation or

    generation, this generator SHALL base every decision about its selected IR

    meaning on the one admitted QSpec FR-330 `ContractPackage` emitted for that

    request. Contract IR owns its lowering and sole strict reader; CG consumes the

    typed admitted value and does not define another package schema or reader.'
- id: interface_001
  path: spec/core/functional/interface-001-codegen-api.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: "```yaml\nname: ContractCodegen\nversion: draft-codegen-v1\ninput:\n  contract_package: public IR BoundPackage\
    \ from the public IR derived executable projection decoder; no private wire or codegen input schema\n  configuration:\
    \ backend selection, customer bindings, output profile\noperations:\n  - name: source_obligation_census\n  \
    \  status: planned; complete producer/consumer implementation gated on IR-759 reviewed neutral correspondence\n\
    \    inputs: [SourceCensusRequest borrowing the selected admitted checked package, complete owner semantic-obligation\
    \ inventory, criterion and production-symbol"
- id: TC-001
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-001-reproducibility.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify repeated generation is byte-identical and every generated Rust family retains its

    input-carried identity, generator name and licensing.'
- id: TC-002
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-002-compile-atomic.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: Verify generated source compiles against only the runtime/customer types and publication is atomic.
- id: TC-003
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-003-unsupported-diagnostics.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify malformed, orphaned, partial, unsupported and undefined-result constructs cannot yield

    complete artifacts or lose their refusal locus.'
- id: TC-007
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-007-cross-backend-parity.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify executable, proptest, Kani, and coverage lowerings agree on the shared bounded corpus and every

    permitted differential fixture has an attributed disposition.'
- id: TC-042
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-042-no-generation-panics.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify the production code under `src/` holds no panic token and that each measured site that a

    test can reach returns its typed value instead of aborting (NFR-005), and that the four index and

    arithmetic sites of IR-577 hold no unchecked index, slice or subtraction.'
- id: TC-052
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-052-fixture-identity.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that the two checked-package fixture builders use Contract IR for

    application identities, use its nominal API for any canonical enum-member

    identity, and preserve admitted packages and stale-key controls.'
- id: TC-053
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-053-contract-package-consumption.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify [FR-039](../functional/FR-039-contract-package-consumption.md) through

    the production negotiation and generation entries using genuine QSL-admitted,

    IR-lowered FR-330 packages. The controls distinguish package decisions from

    decisions the original checked graph or detached lowering records would make.'
- id: TC-054
  path: spec/core/matrix/TC-054-exact-local-protocol-target.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify [FR-039-AC-4](../functional/FR-039-contract-package-consumption.md)

    in two stages. The FR-322-AC-66 worked carrier can exercise the public strict

    reader now; that reader evidence does not establish QSL production or CG

    consumption. The production CG controls require QSL-764 to emit the carrier

    from source, followed by Contract IR lowering into genuine admitted FR-330

    packages. The FR-322 reader owns target admission and located refusals.'
- id: SUR-001
  path: spec/core/matrix/suites.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: '# Contract codegen v0.1 test suites'

  path: spec/core/matrix/tests.md

  path: spec/core/non-functional/NFR-001-reproducible-atomic.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'For one input package, configuration, and supported platform profile, the generator shall emit

    byte-identical bundles and shall publish them atomically without modifying developer-owned regions.'
- id: NFR-002
  path: spec/core/non-functional/NFR-002-provenance-boundary.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: "- Every generated Rust file shall have a header naming `quire-contract-codegen` and every\n  input-carried\

    \ `MIT OR Apache-2.0` SPDX identity.\n- No automated output shall claim project-specific validation, accreditation,\
    \ certification, or human release approval."

  path: spec/core/non-functional/NFR-005-no-generation-panics.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: "- The generator's production code under `src/` shall contain no panic token: no `unwrap`, `expect`,\n\
    \  `unreachable!`, `assert!` or any other call FR-014-AC-39 lists, so that no panic token aborts the\n  generator\
    \ instead of a typed refusal.\n- The sites of the four IR-577 behavior-table rows (in `generate_kani`,\n  `observe_clause`\
    \ and `generate_boolean_oracle_inner`) shall not index, slice or subtract on a\n  value that an earlier function\
    \ establishes.\n- Each of those sites shall read the value with a checked accessor (`get`, a slice pattern,\n\
    \  `checked_sub`, or a value built before it is"
- id: StR-001
  path: spec/core/stakeholder/StR-001-traceable-generation.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Assurance engineers require that the generator shall derive executable, property-test, proof, and

    coverage artifacts reproducibly from one validated contract without hiding unsupported semantics,

    vacuity, rejection, or assumptions.'
- id: ADR-001
  path: spec/decisions/ADR-001-overlapping-generators-and-input-models.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: Accepted.
- id: ADR-002
  path: spec/decisions/ADR-002-backend-adapter-boundary.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: Accepted.

  path: spec/decisions/ADR-003-kani-tractability.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: Accepted.
- id: ADR-004
  path: spec/decisions/ADR-004-generated-subject-abi-open-decisions.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: Accepted.
- id: ADR-005
  path: spec/decisions/ADR-005-original-guardian-gate-ownership.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Proposed. This is an architecture decision for IR-717, not an implemented gate, a conformance

    finding, or permission to activate IR-652 or IR-655. The supported owner API and complete finite

    reserve described below are **UNBACKED**. FR-034 and TC-049 remain the normative contracts.'
- id: ADR-006
  path: spec/decisions/ADR-006-caller-text-admission-boundary.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Proposed. The caller admission oracle and Kani route are unimplemented;

    [FR-035](../oracle/functional/FR-035-caller-text-admission.md) and

    [TC-050](../oracle/matrix/TC-050-caller-text-admission.md) are Planned, not

    proof evidence.'
- id: FR-004
  path: spec/evidence/functional/FR-004-vacuity-evidence.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When LLVM/cargo coverage export and runtime campaign counts are supplied, the generator shall combine

    oracle evaluation, consequent execution, rejection, discard, and test outcome into a deterministic

    per-requirement vacuity report without executing a coverage producer itself.'
- id: FR-036
  path: spec/evidence/functional/FR-036-source-obligation-census.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a source-obligation census is requested, Codegen shall export the complete

    selected obligation inventory, all explicitly mapped criterion-obligation-source-domain

    candidate tuples and unmapped-entity gaps before negotiation, generation or execution.'
- id: TC-006
  path: spec/evidence/matrix/TC-006-vacuity.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify actual generated-oracle probes against native LLVM export, and ultimately keep measured

    coverage, runtime accounting, generated-campaign execution, QSL clause-run outcome, and obligation

    discharge distinct.'
- id: TC-051
  path: spec/evidence/matrix/TC-051-source-obligation-census.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Plan falsifying controls for [FR-036](../functional/FR-036-source-obligation-census.md)

    using genuine typed owner inventories and the reviewed IR-759 correspondence.

    The producer/consumer implementation is Planned under IR-740 and Gated on IR-759;

    these procedures are not executed tests or a claimed proof baseline.'
- id: TM-007
  path: spec/evidence/matrix/tests.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: '# Contract codegen evidence test matrix'
- id: FR-015
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-015-bounded-kani-obligations.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller selects Kani generation for complete-V1 contracts whose scalar

    oracles FR-014 generated, the code generator shall emit one bounded Kani

    obligation per precondition, postcondition, invariant and frame condition,

    each bounded by its model-domain bounds. It is the Kani

    backend''s one generator

    ([ADR-001](../../decisions/ADR-001-overlapping-generators-and-input-models.md)),

    and every item it lowers is a claim over an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2`

    package.'
- id: FR-017
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-017-kani-execution-evidence.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller runs an FR-015, FR-022/FR-014 or FR-035 harness, the code generator shall invoke the

    installed Kani backend and retain the backend''s own reported outcome as typed

    execution evidence. A caller may hand the generator several harnesses to run together

    (FR-017-AC-21 to FR-017-AC-25); the generator then forms groups, runs each

    group in one launcher process, and retains one evidence record per harness. Unless a

    statement says "batch" or "group", it describes a run of one harness.'
- id: FR-025
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-025-generated-subject-abi.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When the code generator emits an [FR-015](./FR-015-bounded-kani-obligations.md) harness, it shall

    emit the harness''s symbolic arguments in the order of the obligation identity''s `arguments`, which

    ascend by identifier. Each argument binding names its parameter node id and declared domain, each

    argument has the Rust type its family''s row below states, and each argument reaches the generated

    oracle widened into the complete-V1 value type without loss.'
- id: FR-028
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-028-bounded-proof-ceilings.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The code generator shall bound every Kani harness so that its run can finish: each harness identity

    records a memory ceiling and a wall-clock ceiling, a run that exceeds either settles `inconclusive`

    with its own reason, and the evidence records the bounds and ceilings the run used. Proof coverage

    is maximised per family. A family proves the production code where its harness verifies within the

    ceilings, and a bounded shadow together with a refinement obligation where it does not

    ([ADR-003](../../decisions/ADR-003-kani-tractability.md)).'
- id: FR-029
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-029-run-outcome-terminal-record.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The Kani adapter shall map every `KaniRunOutcome`, with its inconclusive reason or typed

    cancellation source, paired with the settlement of that run''s replay, to QSL''s FR-331 terminal

    value (`qsl_replay::TerminalValue`) in

    one match with no catch-all arm ([ADR-002](../../decisions/ADR-002-backend-adapter-boundary.md)

    Q3). The map is total over the pair (outcome, replay settlement), not over the outcome alone: a

    falsified run''s value is a function of both, because a counterexample is a refutation only once its

    replay reproduces it. Every pair maps to exactly one terminal value, so every'
- id: FR-030
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-030-ir-outcome-terminal-map.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The generator shall map every Contract IR `KaniOutcome`, paired with the settlement of its replay, to

    exactly one `qsl_replay::TerminalValue`. The map is total over the pair (outcome, replay

    settlement), not over the outcome alone, and it preserves the outcome''s refusal cause: the outcome

    kinds that QSL''s terminal value collapses into one variant stay distinguishable through that

    variant''s typed cause. This is QSL ADR-013 C-09 as merged, whose two inputs are the IR `KaniOutcome`

    and, for a `Counterexample`, the result of its replay. The replay settlement, its six readings and

    the rules'
- id: FR-034
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-034-caller-death-ownership.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'If the original caller dies, then the namespace guardian shall cancel its backend descendants. The

    guardian shall prevent startup EOF from authorizing a production backend instruction.'
- id: FR-040
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-040-cancellation-producer.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller requests cancellation of a bounded Kani execution, the generator SHALL observe the

    caller-owned `quire_exact::Cancel` handle at the real launcher and retain the cause of the first

    cancellation event that stops that launcher. The caller owns the handle and any timer: a timer can

    call `cancel(CancelCause::Deadline)`, while an elapsed [FR-028](./FR-028-bounded-proof-ceilings.md)

    execution ceiling without a recorded cancellation event remains `TimedOut`. This requirement adds

    one producer path to [FR-017](./FR-017-kani-execution-evidence.md); it does not treat a Contract'
- id: FR-041
  path: spec/kani/functional/FR-041-claimed-module-proof-gate.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When the repository claims proof coverage for a generated-harness module, its existing

    [`make kani-gate`](../non-functional/NFR-006-real-kani-lane-gating.md) SHALL accept that claim only

    after a real Kani run discharges a proposition in the module and an executed mutation inside the

    module falsifies a proof check. The gate applies the proof-stage acceptance rule of QSL ADR-011

    §2.3 to CG''s claimed modules. It makes no claim about a module absent from its declared list or

    about a semantic stage the test input did not traverse.'
- id: TC-005
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-005-proof-dependencies.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify generated Kani source, framing, typed bindings, and dependency graphs preserve assumptions and

    block complete-proof claims when required dependencies are not successful. Keep model-domain bounds

    distinct from assumed proof edges.'
- id: TC-014
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-014-numeric-state-kani.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify the generalized Kani adapter derives exact Boolean and bounded-`i64` subject bindings from

    the same checked clauses as executable oracles, constrains symbolic values from IR model domains,

    and emits reproducible proof and counterexample-capable harnesses without widening unsupported input.'
- id: TC-023
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-023-bounded-kani-profile-corpus.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify the current bounded-profile classifier, graph and collection finite-input

    lowerers and corpus emitter against FR-015-AC-82 through

    FR-015-AC-95 and the retirement slices FR-015-AC-109 to FR-015-AC-111. Before AD-004 step 4g, the hand-built
    path''s generated

    `KaniOutcome` is a case classification; after step 4g, generation returns no

    `KaniOutcome`. Only FR-017''s installed-backend run provides proof evidence.

    Each successful case retains a QSL source unit and its imported dependency

    source. The real-Kani lane passes the run''s actual falsification playback

    immediately to the replay'
- id: TC-025
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-025-bounded-kani-obligations.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that bounded contracts produce one harness per obligation kind and

    refuse non-finite obligations. IR-268 covers the collection half of planned V2

    symbolic obligations: the claim is an admitted QSL clause/function body over a

    selected model collection field. Graph reachability is required by

    FR-015-AC-98 and FR-015-AC-105 to FR-015-AC-108 (IR-805); it is not IR-268

    evidence. The finite-input collection and graph corpus is not proof evidence

    for either symbolic family.'
- id: TC-027
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-027-kani-execution-evidence.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that a bounded Kani obligation runs against the installed backend, that

    its outcome is read from the backend rather than defaulted, and that the

    returned evidence describes the invocation that actually happened.'
- id: TC-036
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-036-generated-subject-abi.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that a harness''s symbolic arguments follow its identity''s ascending `arguments` order, that

    each binding names its parameter node id and declared domain, that each family''s argument has its

    stated Rust type and reaches the oracle without loss, and that unbounded and frame obligations

    yield no harness.'
- id: TC-039
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-039-bounded-proof-ceilings.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that every harness identity records its ceilings, that a run exceeding either ceiling settles

    with its own inconclusive reason, that evidence records the bounds and ceilings used, that every

    identity, refusal and evidence names its family, and that the proof subject and a narrowed bound are

    recorded as FR-028 states. Verify the shadow contract (steps 11 to 22): a shadow''s independence from

    the code it stands for, its refinement obligation and the class and strength of its run, the

    abstractions it owes evidence for, its refused shapes, the memory ceiling and the seeded mutants'
- id: TC-040
  path: spec/kani/matrix/TC-040-run-outcome-terminal-record.md

- id: FR-014
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-014-exact-scalar-oracles.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller supplies an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2` package and a set

    of scalar expression nodes, the code generator shall emit a deterministic Rust

    oracle crate whose functions evaluate each node by calling the

    Contract Runtime `exact` operators and metering. It never approximates a

    scalar family through another family and never copies a resource charge.'
- id: FR-018
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-018-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller supplies an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2` package and a set

    of equality expression nodes, the code generator shall emit a deterministic Rust

    oracle crate whose functions decide each node by reconstructing the item''s

    `TypeEnvironment` and calling the Contract Runtime

    `TypeEnvironment::check_equality` and `CheckedEquality::evaluate` with a

    caller-supplied `Meter`. It never compares two values structurally, and never

    copies a resource charge or a planned pair count.'
- id: FR-021
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-021-function-application-oracles.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller supplies an admitted `quire.checked-package/v2` package, function

    bindings and requested `call` nodes, the generator shall classify the admitted

    expression-node graph, build a deterministic, target-neutral instruction

    schedule for each admitted body, and record one generated or typed-refused

    disposition per item. The schedule preserves V2 operation identity, operand

    order, value/result types, function binding, and source occurrence identity;

    it states no charge amount and executes no operation itself. Its body analysis

    and schedule emission use charged iterative walks and'
- id: FR-031
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-031-boolean-oracle-integer-arithmetic.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The Boolean oracle of `interface-001`''s `oracle_slice` lowers one validated Boolean clause over

    Boolean and bounded-integer values into a Rust function. Its clauses may hold integer add,

    subtract, multiply, divide and remainder, and the six integer comparisons. Today the emitter

    renders each of those five operators as the raw Rust infix operator on `i64`, and each comparison

    as the raw infix comparison. It never reads the operand type''s overflow policy. On overflow the

    generated function panics in a debug build and wraps in a release build, and on a zero divisor it

    panics. The exact'
- id: FR-035
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-035-caller-text-admission.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller requests runtime Text admission, the code generator shall emit an

    oracle and a separately bounded Kani obligation for a caller-owned

    `TextPayload` and declared `TextType`. This is a caller-ingress claim, not a

    claim about an expression node in an admitted `CheckedPackageV2`. The oracle

    calls the exact kernel''s `quire_exact::admit_text` API and returns its

    outcome and metering unchanged. Its evidence identifies the caller-declared

    profile, inclusive length bounds, payload class and proof configuration,

    without `ir_confirmed` provenance, a checked node id or a QSL term identity.'
- id: FR-042
  path: spec/oracle/functional/FR-042-generated-checked-invariant-causes.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: The code generator SHALL assign the shared quire-exact typed checked-invariant cause at each generated
    Boolean, equality, function and pre-check placeholder constructor.
- id: TC-024
  path: spec/oracle/matrix/TC-024-exact-scalar-oracles.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that scalar oracles generated from an admitted CheckedPackage V2 cover

    every scalar family, refuse every non-generated item with a typed reason, are

    byte-deterministic, and agree with direct runtime execution. Agreement with the QSL value authority is outside
    CG''s boundary and not claimed by CG (FR-014-AC-47); generated-oracle against QSL agreement is owned by quire-integration
    IR-842.'
- id: TC-029
  path: spec/oracle/matrix/TC-029-composite-equality-oracles.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that composite equality oracles generated from an admitted

    CheckedPackage V2 cover every admitted composite and collection shape, refuse

    every non-generated item with its own typed reason, are byte-deterministic, and

    agree — outcome, admitted charges and consumed counters — with direct runtime

    execution. Agreement with the QSL value authority is outside CG''s boundary and

    not claimed by CG (FR-014-AC-47); it is owned by quire-integration IR-842.'
- id: TC-031
  path: spec/oracle/matrix/TC-031-function-application-oracles.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify CG''s target-neutral function-body graph analysis, flat SSA schedule,

    caller-selected work and source-byte limits, compact location records, typed

    refusals and deterministic claim ordering. Concrete oracle execution is a

    separate leg that CG does not claim: QSL exports no application API through

    qsl-replay (IR-845). The old Contract Runtime `exact` corpus remains historical

    evidence for the behavioral obligations retained in FR-021; it is not a

    required dependency or target path.'
- id: TC-044
  path: spec/oracle/matrix/TC-044-boolean-oracle-integer-arithmetic.md

    outcome refuses'

- id: FR-016
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-016-witness-native-replay.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a FR-015 harness yields a counterexample, the code generator shall decode

    the witness into typed complete-V1 values, validate each value against its

    declared domain, and replay it through native runtime execution before any

    failure is reported.'
- id: FR-024
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-024-counterexample-envelope-intake.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a counterexample is to be replayed, the code generator shall carry it to QSL as QSL''s

    counterexample envelope (`qsl_replay::WitnessEnvelope`), keyed by QSL''s `ObligationIdentity` and

    holding exactly one `qsl_replay::ReplaySource` arm. It shall validate every value against its

    declared domain before any replay, and shall replay only through `qsl_replay::replay`, or through

    `qsl_replay::replay_frame` for a frame counterexample, or through

    `qsl_replay::replay_state_clause` for a postcondition state-clause counterexample.'
- id: FR-032
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-032-routed-scalar-replay-binding.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When the driver requests replay of a routed scalar counterexample, CG shall bind the request

    directly to its `ScalarObligationIdentity`, preserving the arithmetic-parity proposition the

    actual generated harness checked. This requirement owns a public request builder and a public

    settlement converter; the driver owns the intervening QSL replay call. QSL owns the operator-level

    exact evaluation, envelope arm, evidence and terminal causes.'
- id: FR-033
  path: spec/replay/functional/FR-033-composite-parity-replay-binding.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Imported contexts remain PLANNED: the Eq constructor returns typed `ImportedContextUnsupported`

    until CG retains admitted dependency packages from the original compile.'
- id: TC-026
  path: spec/replay/matrix/TC-026-witness-native-replay.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that retained counterexamples are decoded, domain-checked and replayed

    natively before any failure is reported.'
- id: TC-035
  path: spec/replay/matrix/TC-035-counterexample-envelope-intake.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that every counterexample reaches QSL as QSL''s counterexample envelope keyed by QSL''s

    obligation identity, that out-of-domain and incomplete counterexamples are refused before any

    replay, that frame counterexamples carry their QSL identities, that minimization keeps only

    failure-preserving envelopes, and that the generator holds no copy of QSL''s replay types.'
- id: TC-047
  path: spec/replay/matrix/TC-047-routed-scalar-replay-binding.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Planned public-consumer coverage of

    [FR-032](../functional/FR-032-routed-scalar-replay-binding.md), distinguishing lowering parity

    failure from source-property refutation. No implementation or passing replay is claimed. The

    completed CG route is CODE-gated on CG conformance to merged QSL full-claim reports, authoritative scalar

    identity metadata, retained generation/proving context and checked driver-observation contract.

    The measured QSL operator API and scalar terminal causes do not close those gates.'

  path: spec/replay/matrix/TC-048-composite-parity-replay-binding.md

- id: FR-019
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-019-capability-settlement.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a backend provider envelope requests claims of this generator, the

    generator shall settle each requested item at exactly one point, a `negotiate_*`

    arm over a closed backend kind, and shall settle no capability anywhere else.'
- id: FR-022
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-022-routed-generation.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When the orchestrating driver hands this generator the items that FR-019

    settled `supported` and that QSL `route` then routed, each with its request

    index, its routed backend and that backend''s closed backend kind, together

    with one admitted IR `ContractPackageV1` and the complete lowering-position

    mapping, the generator shall run the

    generation arm of each item''s backend kind and return that arm''s output keyed

    by the item''s request index. It shall not settle, select or route a backend

    again.'
- id: FR-026
  path: spec/routed/functional/FR-026-backend-adapter-contract.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The code generator shall hold everything specific to one linked proof backend in that backend''s adapter,

    one implementation of a single adapter trait, and shall reach an adapter only through an exhaustive

    match on the closed `BackendKind` enum

    ([ADR-002](../../decisions/ADR-002-backend-adapter-boundary.md) Q0, Q1 and Q4). ADR-002 Q4 states how a

    second linked backend registers. `Process(BackendId)` has no CG adapter; the

    driver''s plugin host owns its process adapter (QSL ADR-029 PV-4).'
- id: TC-030
  path: spec/routed/matrix/TC-030-capability-settlement.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that every requested capability claim is settled by exactly one

    `negotiate_*` arm over a closed backend kind, that each FR-290 rule settles its

    own row, including whole-envelope refusal for a repeated backend identity.'
- id: TC-033
  path: spec/routed/matrix/TC-033-routed-generation.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that `generate_routed` runs each routed item''s backend-kind generation

    arm, keyed by the driver''s request index. It takes the routed backend and kind

    as given, refuses an inconsistent routing, and returns for Kani exactly what

    the FR-015 generator returns for the same items.'
- id: TC-037
  path: spec/routed/matrix/TC-037-backend-adapter-contract.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that the Kani backend is one implementation of the adapter trait and that the adapter owns its

    execution evidence type.'
- id: TC-046
  path: spec/routed/matrix/TC-046-process-provider-settlement.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that `Process(BackendId)` settles from the FR-331 manifest''s advertised

    (kind, mode) pairs and `domains`, against the requested item''s capability kind

    and full `extent`.

    Manifest `bounds` are run-limit defaults and do not set admission maxima.

    Bounded `ProofBound.kind` is required by QSpec FR-331; QSL-654 owns the

    producer and admit-side `invalid-domains` enforcement. QSpec FR-290-AC-13

    PV-4).'

- id: spec/spec.md
  path: spec/spec.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'This specification defines deterministic lowering from a validated contract package into Rust

    oracles, tri-state test harnesses, shaped proptest strategies, Kani obligations and coverage maps. Generated
    artifacts remain traceable to one authoritative source contract.'
- id: FR-002
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-002-tristate-proptest.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When executable pre/post contracts are lowered, the generator shall emit entry-point harnesses and

    proptest strategies that preserve pass, failed postcondition, and rejected precondition outcomes.'
- id: FR-008
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'For a request selecting one claim of an admitted `CheckedPackageV2`, the generator SHALL use Contract

    IR''s public clause-context integer-comparison operand accessor (IR FR-038-AC-202 through AC-209) to

    admit a direct comparison and derive its exact domains. The generator SHALL return one complete

    strategy bundle or one typed, located refusal; it SHALL NOT generate a partial bundle. This is the

    V2 input contract for the constructive population and campaign behavior of FR-009 through FR-012.

    The IR accessor and its public consumer test are implemented under IR-703 in Contract IR;'
- id: FR-009
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-009-constructive-correlated-populations.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a selected claim of an admitted `CheckedPackageV2` is admitted by

    [FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md), the generator shall emit proptest populations

    that construct every case directly inside the shared domain and on the requested side of the

    relation. A case is a complete valuation of the claim''s reads, including any `Post` read, and its tag

    is the value the selected claim''s V2 comparison oracle (FR-008) returns for that valuation. The

    generator never draws a candidate and then filters it out.'
- id: FR-010
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-010-domain-boundary-campaigns.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a caller requests the `Boundary` population for a selected claim of a `CheckedPackageV2`

    admitted by [FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md), the generator shall emit a finite,

    deterministic census of in-domain cases at the domain edges and the relation''s own edge. Every

    strategy bundle for a selected claim also carries the out-of-domain edge values, so a consumer can

    prove that it refuses them at domain admission. Each in-domain case is tagged with the value the

    selected claim''s V2 comparison oracle (FR-008) returns for it.'
- id: FR-011
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-011-numeric-harness-campaigns.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When a strategy bundle is generated for a selected claim of a `CheckedPackageV2`

    ([FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md)), the generator shall also emit an

    oracle-conformance campaign runner. The runner evaluates the selected claim''s V2 comparison oracle

    on each generated valuation, records the runtime verdict for the checked clause kind, and requires

    that verdict to equal the case''s

    expectation. Its summary reports the discard rate and the rejection rate as exact counts, or as

    unavailable when a counter may be saturated.'
- id: FR-012
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-012-constraint-preserving-shrinking.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'When proptest shrinks a failing case drawn from a `Satisfying`, `Violating`, or `Broad` population of

    a selected V2 claim ([FR-008](./FR-008-bound-domain-strategy-admission.md)), every candidate it visits shall
    stay inside the shared domain and keep the expectation tag

    of the case it came from. This refines [FR-002](./FR-002-tristate-proptest.md) FR-002-AC-4 for the

    populations of a selected V2 claim; FR-002-AC-4 itself stays verified by TC-004.'
- id: FR-013
  path: spec/strategy/functional/FR-013-it010-consumable-output.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The generator shall deliver bound strategy, census, and runner output as typed generated Rust, so a

    downstream crate can place every case''s values into its own runtime inputs by typed declaration identity, selected
    path and observation. The generator shall not

    require any serialized case format or schema owned by this repository for that consumption.'
- id: TC-004
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/TC-004-proptest-strategies.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify generated harnesses preserve tri-state outcomes and strategy construction/shrinking respects

    supported constraints and boundaries.'
- id: TC-017
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/TC-017-bound-domain-admission.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify selected-claim V2 strategy admission through IR''s public clause-context comparison accessor,

    exact domain checks, first-defect diagnostics and atomic bundle output. This case is planned until

    CG''s V2 strategy implementation, V2 comparison oracle and a CG-side real QSL ConfigVersion V2

    producer fixture exist; IR-703''s public accessor is implemented in Contract IR.'
- id: TC-018
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/TC-018-constructive-correlated-populations.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that populations for a selected V2 claim (FR-008) are constructed rather than filtered,

    generate exactly the true value sets, refuse empty sides explicitly, and handle `i64` extremes

    without overflow. Every fixture is an IR-admitted `CheckedPackageV2` with a selected clause id and

    authentic claim occurrence; synthetic topology fixtures are labelled and do not stand in for the

    QSL-produced ConfigVersion control.'
- id: TC-019
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/TC-019-domain-boundary-campaigns.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that the generated in-domain census, out-of-domain array, and unrepresentable-edge array hold

    exactly the cases FR-010 defines, in order, with correct tags and bounded size.'
- id: TC-020
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/TC-020-numeric-harness-campaigns.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that the generated conformance runner maps oracle results to verdicts by clause kind, records

    them without global rejects, runs the census exhaustively, detects oracle disagreement, and reports

    exact rates.'
- id: TC-021
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/TC-021-constraint-preserving-shrinking.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that every candidate proptest visits while shrinking a population of a selected V2 claim

    (FR-008) stays in domain and

    keeps its original tag, that `Broad` never shrinks across sides, and that shrink replays are counted.'
- id: TC-022
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/TC-022-it010-consumable-output.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Verify that a downstream crate can include and compile the generated bound-strategy Rust source

    with only `proptest` and `quire-contract-runtime` as manifest dependencies. Verify that its header

    names the source clause and no local serialized format exists.'
- id: TM-002
  path: spec/strategy/matrix/tests.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: '# Contract codegen strategy test matrix'
- id: NFR-004
  path: spec/strategy/non-functional/NFR-004-constructive-generation-efficiency.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'The generated strategies and conformance runner for a selected V2 claim shall produce every requested
    case without

    discards, proptest global rejects, or framework exhaustion, and the boundary census shall stay small

    enough to evaluate exhaustively.'
- id: TM-008
  path: spec/tests.md
  role: context_only
  excerpt: 'Each subsystem owns one matrix beside its requirements, per

    `quire-contract-ir:ADR-0056`, whose registry is in [spec.md](./spec.md). This index declares no test case; the
    matrices are the coverage authority.'

  path: src/core/artifact.rs
  role: examined
  excerpt: "//! Generated files and the validated bundle every generator builds (AD-004 step 2a).\n//!\n//! This\

    ## Hash / digest / pin antipattern: do not introduce


    Hashes, digests, SHAs, pins, checksum catalogs and records that track files, versions or

    tools are an antipattern and have been removed from this repository. Do not introduce

    any new use of them. If you find one, remove it as part of the change. The only hash

    proved. Package versions live in Cargo.toml / package.json and their lockfiles'
